field_overlap.anfc_label_type: object detection / instance segmentation boxes and masks over vessel classes -- NOT the 21 clinical fields
field_overlap.shared_field_explanation: ZERO clinical fields are shared. ANFC carries per-vessel geometry classes (capillary/abnormal/aggregation/blur/hemo/normal); the hospital cohort carries exam-level clinical answers. They are not the same label space, so ANFC cannot be an external test set for any of the 21 fields. It was only ever used to train a detector/segmenter whose outputs became features.
field_overlap.doctor_annotation_label_type: per-image vessel annotations on a subset of the SAME hospital exams -- so it overlaps the hospital set at exam level but adds no new exams and no new clinical fields

acquisition_conditions.manifest_columns_for_device_magnificatio: ABSENT -- no such column exists in the manifest (102 columns, all listed in the group-1 artifact)
acquisition_conditions.exif: EMPTY -- no EXIF tags on any sampled cap_image
acquisition_conditions.device: UNVERIFIED -- no 仪器/型号/设备/显微 string in any of 461 reports, no EXIF, no manifest column

magnification.note: these are regex hits for <number>倍/x and may be text about vessel counts rather than optics; none is a reliable magnification record

finger.status: PARTIALLY RECORDED -- present in the report text of a MINORITY of exams only
finger.note: coverage is far too low and too irregular to stratify any result by finger; and the mention is free text in the report body, not a structured field

acquisition_conditions.site: UNVERIFIED as a structured field; 甲襞 appears in report text but identifies the examination type, not a per-image site
acquisition_conditions.protocol: UNVERIFIED -- no written acquisition protocol exists in the repository
acquisition_conditions.verdict: Acquisition metadata is essentially NOT RECORDED. Device, magnification and protocol: nothing, in the manifest, in EXIF (empty on every sampled image) or in the report text. Finger/hand: mentioned in free text for a small minority of exams, not structured, not usable for stratification. All 2207 images are 1024x768 and named CAPorg<n>.jpg, which is consistent with one capture software but does NOT prove one device or one magnification. CONSEQUENCES: (1) no result in this project can be stratified by device, magnification or finger; (2) the micron scale cannot be recovered from acquisition settings, which is why um_per_pixel had to be back-fitted from labels and is not usable as calibration; (3) 'same device' cannot be asserted in any launch material.

q1_split_unit.patient_id_verdict: patient_id is 100% EMPTY -- patient identity CANNOT be verified from the manifest. If any patient contributed two exams, that is undetectable here and would be a real (unquantified) leak.
q1_split_unit.duplicate_group_semantics: unions exams sharing a byte-identical image (sha256), NOT patients; see build_splits.py

q2_exact_duplicates.verdict: no exact-duplicate leakage among real images

blank_images.note: asymmetric: development was trained and scored with these rows, locked has none. Cost measured separately in artifacts/experiments/blank_audit_20260919/blank_audit.json (delta shifts of only -0.005 to +0.011)

q3_near_duplicate_leakage.verdict: no near-duplicate leakage: locked images are no closer to development than development images are to each other (difference ~+0.001, and 0 locked images exceed 0.98 cosine while the matched dev control reaches 1.000 because of the blank placeholders)

with_blanks.auroc_note: 0.5 would mean the encoder cannot tell two images of one exam from two images of different exams

blanks_excluded.auroc_note: 0.5 would mean the encoder cannot tell two images of one exam from two images of different exams

q4_does_encoder_separate_exams.why_both: the 21 blank images are mutual duplicates, so they inflate nearest-neighbour statistics and can make the encoder look unable to separate exams. The blanks_excluded row is the correct one to read.

limitations: patient identity is unverifiable: patient_id is empty for all 233 rows. Everything here is at EXAM level. If one patient contributed two exams that landed on opposite sides, this audit cannot detect it
near-duplicate search uses DINOv2 mean-pooled features, which is the same representation the classifier sees -- appropriate for leakage, but it is not a pixel-level or acquisition-metadata check
single encoder, single pooling (mean) for the similarity analysis

split_is_by_patient.answer: NO -- it is by EXAM (exam_case_id), not by patient. Patient identity cannot be checked at all because patient_id is null for all 233 rows.
split_is_by_patient.what_was_verified_instead: 0 exams and 0 duplicate_groups span the split; 0 of 2089 image hashes are shared across it; and a matched near-duplicate control shows locked images are no closer to development images (0.9217) than development images are to each other (0.9207). See split_integrity above.
split_is_by_patient.residual_risk: If the same person was examined twice, their two exams could land on opposite sides of the split and I would not detect it. This is UNQUANTIFIED.
